# Worked recording directions

These examples demonstrate specificity. Confirm capabilities and actual controls
against the supplied product; the examples do not authorize recording or writes.

## Whole-product introduction before the individual shot

For an Agent-driven business app, first decide what the viewer must learn:
business language creates related structure; real content feeds useful views;
another instruction changes those views; a new collection need extends the same
application. A polished form-submission take cannot replace this introduction.

An illustrative continuous business task:

| Scene | Product change and exact proposed input | Audience explanation | Required reveal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create | "Build a store workspace with linked products, suppliers, purchases and orders. Create structure only." | "Describe what the store manages; the Agent creates the related business tables." | Actual request precedes new tables and relationships |
| Populate | "Add the supplied synthetic data to those tables and link it by business IDs." | "Bring the business records into that structure, so orders and products connect." | Actual supported data operation, not silently substituted prefilled tables |
| Visualize | "Show product categories, purchase status and daily orders using this application's data." | "Turn the questions you care about into views of the same business data." | Real generated views, not merely opening an existing dashboard |
| Revise | "Add an order-status view to this dashboard and keep the existing charts." | "Ask for another perspective; the current dashboard changes without starting over." | Same dashboard before/after, preserved widgets and requested addition |
| Extend | "Create an order form against the existing orders with product, quantity and contact fields." | "A new collection need becomes an entry point connected to the system you already built." | Form creation and binding; publication/sharing only within authorized scope |

These are planned commands, not claims of verified prompt success. Specific
chart types, import routes and publication rules need evidence and rehearsal.
If an unsupported funnel is requested, verify or explicitly propose a supported
status view; preserve conversational revision rather than fake a funnel.
Do not quietly substitute unrelated manual editing footage.

Narration deliberately names capabilities and mechanisms. It does not enumerate
field counts, read HTTP responses, or rely on "powerful" and "efficient." The
following detailed examples explain how to capture such reveals; a single one
of them does not constitute the entire product introduction.

## Agent creates a business table

Goal: "Present Biz Table to LT, about one minute."
Illustrative section budget: about 18 seconds in the edit, **not** an observed
generation time. Use one coherent table across later form/dashboard sections.

### Initial state and preparation

- Actual product homepage; test application contains no business tables.
- Connected Agent is visible beside the product or captured separately.
- Connection and login are prepared before capture; no secret or tenant detail
  appears. The table itself must be created during capture.

### Ordered recording script

| Beat | Record | Presentation / voice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Establish | Product homepage and empty app | Wide shot. Say: "Describe the work your team needs to manage." No success overlay |
| Input | Type: `Create a Requests table with Request title, Priority (High/Medium/Low), Status (New/In review/Decided), Team and Description. Do not add records.` | Push toward the composer only after orientation. Show full input long enough to read. Copy: "Create a table from a request" |
| Execute | Send once; retain the sent message and actual working state | Return to Agent/product overview. Say: "Describe the structure, and the Agent creates the table." |
| Wait/edit | Real execution until completion | Keep onset and completion; remove uneventful middle waiting if too long and label "Waiting shortened." Do not animate a fake progress bar |
| Result | Open the new table; show all five headers and zero records | Gentle push to headers, keeping table name. The empty-record check stays in production notes. Say: "That request becomes a structured workspace you can continue using." Copy: "From a request to a working table" only after verified creation |
| Handoff | Keep the empty table visible | Pull back toward the form entry for the next section. Do not reveal prepared sample rows without a labeled transition |

### Verify and stop conditions

The exact tool result/structure readback must match the requested columns,
options and zero rows. If the Agent fails or returns a partial structure, stop
and capture the failure; do not reveal a prepared successful table instead.
If the request timed out after writing, read back before sending it again.

## Same product, supporting form submission section

This is a focused collection proof, not evidence of Agent-created forms or a
complete product introduction. If conversational form creation is must-show,
record the creation request and generated form before this sequence.

Prepared before capture: a published test form bound to the same table and six
synthetic records. Announce this setup transition; do not claim the build shot
included it.

Exact input:

```text
Request title: Weekly request summary
Priority: High
Status: New
Team: Operations
Description: Consolidate team requests for the weekly leadership review.
```

Sequence:

1. Open the actual form. Keep labels and Submit visible.
2. Fill in order; one subtle highlight follows the active field.
3. Hold the completed form for reading; remove highlights before Submit.
4. Submit **once**. Keep the genuine success response on screen.
5. Return to the same table; locate the new item using the returned ID or
   discriminating fields. Compare title, priority and team.
6. Show the count changing from six to seven only if actual readback confirms it.

Voice:
> "Team members can submit requests through a form. The new item appears in the
> same table, ready to be reviewed."

Screen copy: "Collect a request" during entry; replace with "Saved to the table"
only after verification. If the next section is a dashboard, follow this same
record into its actual aggregation rather than changing datasets.

## Non-table product: transcript-based audio editing

Assumed verified features: transcript editing and file export.
User goal: a short product introduction for podcast creators.

Preparation: authorized synthetic recording with the line
"The meeting is Tuesday. Sorry, the meeting is Thursday." Save a copy; never
edit the only original source.

1. **Initial**: actual editor project, full waveform and synchronized transcript.
2. **Input/action**: select exactly "The meeting is Tuesday. Sorry," using the
   product's documented transcript-edit action; remove that audio interval.
3. **Result**: the remaining transcript is "the meeting is Thursday." Play the
   edit across its boundary to verify a clean cut. Keep transport and playhead
   visible; do not overlay a fabricated waveform.
4. **Camera/highlight**: begin wide; push toward the selected phrase before
   deletion; remove its highlight when deleted; pull back to show playback.
5. **Sound**: let the before/after spoken audio play without narration over it.
   Then say, "Edit the words and check the change in the recording."
6. **Export**: use the actual export dialog and chosen documented format; show
   completion and open/probe the exported file.
7. **Editing**: long encoding waits may be cut; retain export request and the
   real resulting artifact. Screen copy: "Edit by transcript," then "Exported"
   only after the file exists and plays.

A sentence about editing is not enough: the phrase, action, playback boundary
and output verification are the substance of the recording script.

## Missing custom feature

User adds "AI forecasts next month's demand" but the supplied repo only supports
manual aggregation.

Wrong: invent a forecast button, sample curve and upbeat narration.

Right: retain the feature section as blocked and ask for the source/UI that
implements forecasting. State the proposed proof requirement: a supported input,
real generated forecast, displayed uncertainty and a result that can be inspected.
Do not invent the command or call this section recordable yet.

## Compact default presentation

Use a concise flow or a selected-step workspace, not every field at once. Show:

1. Initial state -> ordered actions -> end screen.
2. Verbatim input and waiting/edit decisions.
3. Highlight, framing, voice and on-screen copy.
4. Verification and handoff.

The user can accept the Agent's complete draft and continue; they do not have to
fill these fields one by one. Do not add extra confirmations merely because the
form has many fields. Required approval and execution permissions still apply.

## Tool-aware first cut: Agent builds a table

The following is an **illustrative editing plan**, not measured footage or a
claim of an installed OpenScreen version. Preserve a clean source take and bind
the events to times after capture. The product screen never gets reconstructed.

| Retained event | Capture instructions | Viewer's focus and editor instruction | Audio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homepage established | Record product identity and empty test workspace | Wide view, no zoom/highlight yet | "Describe the work your team needs to manage." |
| Full prompt visible | Type the exact prompt above into the connected Agent | Smooth push toward composer; keep complete prompt and Send; hold to read | "The Agent turns that request into a structured table." |
| Send / work begins | Send once and keep the real sent message plus execution onset | Remove input outline; hold shared Agent/product framing | Finish the input sentence; do not fill the entire raw wait with speech |
| Work interval | Continue recording or preserve timestamped completion in a separately authorized take | Cut the uneventful middle, not every instant of causal context; show "Waiting shortened" at the join if needed | Remove mic silence; relocate voiceover to the retained completion |
| Table ready | Open the real new table; verify headers and zero records | Start wide, ease toward key headers; keep table name | Finish the capability sentence while its result appears; do not read the verification count |
| Result readable | Keep the result stable while it is inspected | Once the camera settles, outline Priority; remove before pullback | Screen copy: "A workspace built from your request" only after verified creation |
| Handoff | End on a stable overview | Pull back and position the next entry in frame; no simultaneous new caption and zoom | End narration before changing context |

### Bind this to the tool rather than saying "add effects"

- **OpenScreen candidate path:** select the authorized window; record to a native
  project; use its verified manual zoom regions and timeline trims; represent
  emphasis with supported annotations. If the installed version cannot produce
  the intended outline, explicitly hand it to a verified compositor/manual edit.
- **Browser-only candidate path:** automate real inputs with inspected targets
  and capture WebM; use supported cursor/highlight controls if the installed
  recorder has them. Editorial zoom and cuts belong to a verified post-processing
  stage if absent from capture. No claim that every Playwright version exposes
  the researched `page.screencast` APIs.
- Do not use auto-zoom's entire proposed sequence without review: exclude
  incidental mouse moves, leave enough context, and coordinate with captions.
- Resolve actual region bounds from the real take and keep one coordinate
  convention. Re-map annotations if the frame is cropped or scaled.

### Why a raw 60-second take need not become a 60-second video

Hypothetical measured source after a rehearsal:

| Source time | Content | Edit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0–3 s | Homepage | Keep |
| 3–8 s | Prompt and Send | Keep |
| 8–10 s | Execution begins | Keep |
| 10–50 s | Unchanging working indicator | Cut |
| 50–54 s | Completion and opening the new table | Keep |
| 54–60 s | Readable verified table | Keep |

This cut is **20 seconds**, before any added transitions/holds. A highlight at
source 54 s now begins at output 14 s, not 54 s. Narration for the result belongs
over that retained result, not the removed 40-second wait. No speed multiplier
is needed just to get rid of a static spinner. Real durations must come from
the actual recording; do not put these hypothetical numbers into runtime claims.
